A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Thera research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and matchable despite substantial reformatting and appendix renumbering.

before.justification: V3 reports original super-resolution benchmarks, component ablations, qualitative reconstructions, and COZ optical-zoom experiments in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V4 retains those empirical results and adds gradient-quality measurements, repeated-run variability, frequency-bank fitting experiments, and runtime/memory measurements.

M1.justification: The stated diffusivity initialization in Appendix A.2 changes from sqrt(ln(4))/(2*pi^2) to ln(4)/(2*pi^2). This revises a parameter prescription; the thermal-field architecture, TV objective, hypernetwork variants, and Thera++ adaptation remain unchanged.

E1.justification: V4 Appendix D adds frozen-frequency-bank reconstruction experiments on retained natural-image datasets and a fastMRI single-coil knee validation subset. This introduces medical-image coverage and a distinct fitting scenario, but does not evaluate end-to-end MRI super-resolution. Existing SR datasets and COZ coverage are retained.

E2.justification: Matched experiments retain their comparator membership, including the COZ LIT and LMI rows. The new GMSD and runtime comparisons reuse previously evaluated methods; the abbreviated Ciao label corresponds to CiaoSR.

E3.justification: V4 adds GMSD evaluation, frozen-bank fitting with AdamW for 600 iterations across five local-field sizes, and controlled runtime/VRAM evaluation using 48×48 inputs at ×4 scaling. The fixed-diffusivity setting also follows the corrected formula. These substantially extend evaluation procedures while retaining the main training regimen.

E4.justification: New Appendix D examines learned frequency distributions, reconstruction with a frozen frequency bank across datasets and field sizes, and converged diffusivity relative to its theoretical value. Appendix F adds computational-efficiency analysis. Existing component ablations remain, with revised fixed-diffusivity results.

E5.justification: V3 provides no comparable run-count or uncertainty reporting. V4 Appendix C.3 reports three differently seeded training runs, PSNR standard deviations in Table 7, and Thera Pro SSIM/GMSD deviations in Tables 4–5. This establishes new uncertainty reporting, without establishing an increase from a previously known run count.

E6.justification: Main PSNR tables, retained SSIM values, out-of-distribution benchmark scores, and COZ scores are unchanged. Table 3 revises four diffusivity-related rows: for example, ×2-only training evaluated at ×6 changes from 26.47 to 26.34 dB under the revised diffusivity prescription. New Tables 5 and 8–10 substantially add gradient-quality, reconstruction-error, converged-diffusivity, and computational-cost results.

T1.justification: Equations 3, 12, and 13 correct the diffusivity calculation: ln(4) replaces sqrt(ln(4)), and Equation 3 squares the sampling rate in the denominator. These repair limited algebraic inconsistencies; the heat-equation construction, Gaussian observation model, and t=S^2 relationship are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain their principal claims. The introduction adds an explicit data-efficiency claim: analytically handling scale is said to reduce data requirements by fitting a 2D field instead of learning a 3D spatial-and-scale field.

C2.justification: V4 interprets the learned frequency bank as a general-purpose dictionary and explains learned diffusivity values around half the Gaussian prescription through the Mitchell–Netravali downsampling mismatch. It also discusses the perception–distortion tradeoff behind choosing pixel fidelity. The existing architectural limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V4 documents fastMRI intensity normalization, frozen-bank fitting settings including AdamW and learning rate 0.001, and RTX 3090 Ti hardware for timing measurements. It identifies the training downsampling filter more precisely. Main training details, hypernetwork specifications, and project-access information are largely retained.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 adds positioning against generative/diffusion SR, citing Saharia, Gao, Blau and Michaeli, and Delbracio and Milanfar. Xue et al. and Zbontar et al. are added for GMSD and fastMRI. The established relationship to neural-field ASR methods remains.

P1.justification: Most existing prose is retained, with focused explanations of time, diffusivity, and the backbone–hypernetwork interface. V4 reorders qualitative and quantitative discussion, moves references before the appendices, expands author information, and changes citation style.

P2.justification: V4 replaces the two-column format with a single-column template, substantially changing typography, figure/table placement, sizing, and caption layout throughout. It also adds frequency-distribution Figure 11, five new tables, and uncertainty rows in Table 4.

improvement.justification: The corrected diffusivity calculation improves mathematical consistency, while variability estimates, diagnostic experiments, and computational measurements make the existing conclusions easier to assess. These provide targeted gains in correctness and empirical transparency around largely retained principal results and limitations.
